assumptions: Every candidate is fitted on ONE shared topology, so only the model varies.
limits: A ranking among the candidates fitted, not a claim that the best one is adequate.
A log-likelihood measured on a different topology answers a different question and is not comparable.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which substitution model do these data prefer, by AIC, AICc or BIC with Akaike weights?

description: Choose the substitution model for a maximum-likelihood phylogeny by fitting every candidate — model x rate-heterogeneity x invariant-sites — on ONE shared topology and ranking them by AIC, AICc or BIC with Akaike weights. Fitting on a shared topology is the point: a model test that also searched topologies would vary two things at once, and a log-likelihood measured on a different tree answers a different question. Wire the winning model into build_tree's `ml_model`.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

criterion.description: which information criterion ranks the table. Changing it re-ranks candidates that are already fitted — it does not re-fit them.

gamma_categories.description: discrete-Γ category counts to try. `[1]` is no rate heterogeneity; `[1, 4]` is the usual sweep and is the panel's default.

include_invariant.description: also try each model with a proportion of invariant sites (+I), doubling the candidate count.

models.description: candidate substitution models. Every one is fitted; the sweep costs one ML optimisation per candidate.

sequences.description: aligned sequences — wire align_sequences' rows here, or name library documents.

name: select_substitution_model

best.description: the winning model in the conventional shorthand (e.g. `GTR+G4+I`)

fits.description: every candidate with its log-likelihood, free parameters, AIC/AICc/BIC and Akaike weight

startingTree.description: the ONE topology every candidate was fitted on, in Newick — reported because it is a shared assumption of the whole table

weight.description: the winner's Akaike weight — the share of the evidence it carries. A low weight means the data do not choose between the top models, which is a finding and not a failure
